units.text: INT. TOLL PLAZA - BOOTH 4 - NIGHT
A glass cubicle on an empty highway.
A space heater ticks.
A thermos, a paperback, a laminated sign reading EXACT CHANGE.
WEN DAI (50s, reading glasses on a beaded chain) marks her page and slides the window open as headlights arrive.
PRAKASH NAIR (30s, rumpled suit, a sleeping toddler visible in the car seat behind him) hands her a twenty.
She makes change slowly, counting it out coin by coin.
Long drive?
units.name: WEN

units.text: Not too bad.
units.name: PRAKASH

units.text: His hands stay on the wheel at ten and two.
She hands him the coins.
He puts them in the cup holder one at a time.
A phone rings in the booth.
Wen picks it up.
Wen, it's Ngozi at the state barracks. Is a grey Corolla at your gate?
units.name: MRS. OKAFOR

units.text: Wen looks at the grey Corolla.
She looks at the toddler.
She looks at Prakash's hands.
No. Quiet night. I'll call you back.
units.name: WEN

units.text: She hangs up.
Prakash has not moved.
Your tail light is out. Take the service road. The patrol doesn't run it.
units.name: WEN

units.text: He stares at her.
She slides the window shut and opens her paperback.
